name: How do you choose a general contractor for a new commercial build?

mainEntity.name: What should owners look for when hiring a general contractor for ground-up commercial construction in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What should owners look for when hiring a general contractor for ground-up commercial construction in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hiring the right general contractor is one of the most important decisions on a ground-up commercial project. Owners should look beyond price and evaluate relevant project experience, local permitting knowledge, financial stability, communication style, and subcontractor network. A contractor who has successfully completed similar work in Los Angeles is more likely to understand city review cycles, utility coordination, and site constraints. Ask to see examples of comparable projects, current workload, and references from owners or developers with similar budgets and timelines. The contractor should be able to explain how they manage preconstruction, long-lead items, change orders, inspections, and closeout. It is also worth asking who will actually run the job day to day, since the person selling the work is not always the person managing it. The cheapest bid can be a red flag if it excludes sitework, permitting tasks, or realistic contingency. A better contractor provides a clear scope, a believable schedule, and a practical plan for risks. For urban projects in Glendale, Pasadena, Burbank, or North Hollywood, local execution skill often matters more than broad marketing claims.
acceptedAnswer.description: Choose a contractor with local permit experience, strong subcontractor relationships, realistic scheduling, and proven work on similar building types. Ask how they handle change orders, long-lead materials, utility coordination, and city inspections. The best contractor is not just the lowest bidder but the one who can deliver the full scope with fewer surprises.
